lessons.title: Basic Terminology and Concepts
lessons.section: What will you learn in this course?
lessons.content:
Basic Terminology and Concepts in Short Strangle

1. Short Strangle: A short strangle involves selling both a call and a put option on the same underlying asset, with different strike prices but the same expiration date.

2. Call Option: A contract that gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy an underlying asset at a specified strike price before or at expiration.

3. Put Option: A contract that gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to sell an underlying asset at a specified strike price before or at expiration.

4. Strike Price: The predetermined price at which the underlying asset can be bought or sold when exercising an option.

5. Expiration Date: The final date on which the option contract remains valid.

6. Premium: The amount received by the option seller for writing the option.

7. Out-of-the-Money (OTM): For a call, the strike is above the underlying price; for a put, the strike is below the underlying price.

8. Breakeven Points: The approximate upper and lower prices at expiration where the total premium offsets losses.

9. Implied Volatility: The market's expectation of future volatility embedded in option prices.

10. Time Decay: The erosion of option value as expiration approaches, commonly measured by Theta.

11. Assignment: The obligation of an option seller to fulfill the terms of the option when exercised.

12. Margin: Capital required by the broker to support the risk of the short option position.

Correlation Table Stocks
lessons.content:
Explanation of Correlation Table

The correlation table provides insight into the relationship between different securities and the broader market. Correlation values range from -1 to +1. A value near +1 means two securities tend to move together, while a value near -1 means they tend to move in opposite directions. Values closer to zero indicate weaker relationships.

Use correlation as one input when evaluating portfolio diversification and concentration risk. Highly correlated positions can behave like one large exposure during major market moves.

lessons.title: Correlation Table ETF
lessons.content:
Detailed Correlation Table

This lesson reviews ETF correlation as a portfolio-management tool. Correlation can help estimate how closely holdings may move together and where diversification may be weaker than it first appears.

Compare broad-market, sector and asset-class ETFs to understand whether a collection of positions represents genuinely different risks or multiple expressions of the same market exposure.

Managing Emotions in Trading
lessons.content:
Understanding Common Trading Emotions

Fear, greed, frustration and overconfidence can all interfere with a trading plan. A structured process helps separate decisions from short-term emotion.

Define risk, position size, adjustment rules and exit criteria before entering a trade. Use a journal to compare planned actions with actual behavior.

lessons.title: Developing Discipline
lessons.content:
Developing Discipline in Trading

Create a comprehensive trading plan with entry criteria, risk limits, position sizing, adjustments and exit rules. Discipline means following that process consistently, especially when a position becomes uncomfortable.

lessons.title: Building Confidence through Practice
lessons.content:
Building Confidence through Practice

Confidence should come from education, repetition and measured experience rather than from a single winning trade. Practice the strategy, review outcomes, and refine your process over time.

lessons.title: Stress Management Techniques
lessons.content:
Stress Management Techniques in Trading

Identify the sources of trading stress and reduce unnecessary pressure with appropriate position size, defined risk, planned adjustments and realistic expectations.

lessons.title: Mastering the Psychology of Short Straddle Trading
lessons.content:
Mastering the Psychology of Short Straddle Trading

Short premium strategies require patience, discipline and a clear understanding of risk. Focus on process, maintain consistency and avoid emotional changes to the plan that are not supported by the trade thesis.

lessons.title: Trading Options with Fearlessness and Confidence
Course Summary
lessons.content:
Course Summary

This course has provided an in-depth exploration of the Short Strangle strategy, a non-directional options strategy designed to benefit from premium decay when the underlying remains within a favorable range.

You reviewed market conditions, volatility, Vega, Theta, Delta, construction, order execution, risk management, adjustments, diversification, advanced combinations and trading psychology. Use these concepts together as one structured decision-making process.
